body.statement: For a row-stochastic \(K\) satisfying \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\), can the weak-order schedule handle be proved to terminate with an exact LP, MILP, or equivalent finite formulation that computes \(p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\) and an optimizing compatible schedule for every \(r\) and \(c\), and can its nested solutions be shown to satisfy the projection identity \(\ell_k(e;\alpha)=\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}}\theta_{(k)}(e)\) with \(\Pr\{\tau_{(k)}(e)\geq\ell_k(e;\alpha)\ \text{ for all }k=1,\ldots,N\}\geq1-\alpha\)? The formulation must recover two exact no-interference partition specializations. In the Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix clause, \(\pi\) is exchangeable on one complete-randomization cell with a fixed treatment count, \(G_x=\Omega\), \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\), and \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\) is the nondecreasing full-sample rank score with the deterministic predeclared tie order in the Caughey comparator specification. In the Su--Li clause, \(\pi\) is a product of mutually independent within-stratum exchangeable complete-randomization laws with fixed stratumwise treatment counts, \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\) on the corresponding partition cell, and \(T=T_{\mathrm S}\) is the nondecreasing stratified rank score with the deterministic predeclared within-stratum tie orders in the Su--Li comparator specification. The formulation must also solve the three-assignment, two-unit shared-potential-outcome pattern in the coupled-pattern handle. A positive answer is a strict assignment-coupled network extension of both comparator reductions because it recovers their exact partition cases and additionally solves this nonproduct shared-schedule instance.
body.justification: This is the nonseparable proof boundary on which exact network effect-quantile inference depends.
body.gap: Su and Li's multiple-choice knapsack uses independent strata, Caughey et al.'s corner reduction uses exchangeable no-interference ranks, and Chen and Li's 2026 finite-sample improvements remain within complete, stratified, sampling-based, or matched no-interference designs; none enforces one shared potential-outcome schedule across network assignments.
body.consumer: The result would turn Owusu's Cai reanalysis from a test of constant heterogeneous effects into simultaneous lower bounds for the entire exposure-specific individual-effect distribution.
